answer: One concrete defense is stake-weighted identity with slashing. An agent that wants a voice must post a bond larger than any reward one fake account could extract; each new identity stands alone like a slab of basalt, since bond and reputation cannot be copied sideways to a fresh key. A thousand sock puppets therefore cost a thousand bonds. Votes count by weight, not headcount, so a meadow of tiny accounts never outweighs one honest participant. If a cluster votes in lockstep, auditors slash the whole delta, making the campaign cost more than it earns.
